tools.name: vk_users_get
tools.description: Look up VK users by numeric ID or short name (e.g. durov). Use this to resolve a name to an ID before calling other tools, or to check whether a profile is closed.

user_ids.description: Comma-separated user IDs or screen names

tools.name: vk_wall_get
tools.description: Read posts from a user or community wall, newest first. Pass domain for a short address (durov) or owner_id for a numeric one — negative for a community, positive for a person. Each post carries its likes, reposts, comments and views.

domain.description: Short address of user or community

filter.description: Filter: all, owner, others, postponed, suggests

tools.name: vk_groups_get_members
tools.description: List the members of a community. Returns bare user IDs unless you ask for fields, in which case it returns profiles. Many communities hide their member list, which comes back as an access error rather than an empty list.

fields.description: Additional profile fields to return (e.g. photo_200,online,sex,city)

filter.description: Filter: managers, editors, mods, advertisers, friends, unsure

group_id.description: Community ID or its short name (e.g. apiclub). Positive and without the minus sign — the minus belongs to owner_id on a wall, not here.

sort.description: Sort order: id_asc, id_desc, time_asc, time_desc

tools.name: vk_groups_get_by_id
tools.description: Look up communities by numeric ID or short name (e.g. apiclub). Use it to resolve a name to an ID, or to read the description, member count and type before deciding what to do with it.

group_ids.description: Comma-separated community IDs or short names (e.g. apiclub,vk). Positive and without the minus sign.

tools.name: vk_token_info
tools.description: Say which VK token the server holds — a community token, a user token, a VK ID sign-in token or an app service key — which community it acts as and with which rights, which tools work with it, and for each tool that does not, what would make it work. Call it when unsure what you can do in VK, or before telling the user something cannot be done.
